get.summary:
`GET /apps` — the full registry in display order. Scope-gated on
`wildflower/Apps.r` through [`Scoped<LiveAppsReader>`]; the host wraps the router
with the bearer gate that inserts the caller's scope claims.

200.description: Every app in the registry, ordered by position

post.summary:
`POST /apps/{id}` — launch an app (`404` if no app has this id). Every owner UI
drives this through the typed client so the owner bearer rides along.
Scope-gated on the `wildflower/launch` umbrella through
[`Scoped<LiveAppLauncher>`]; a SMART app additionally requires the caller's grant
to cover its OAuth client's scopes (checked in [`launch`]). See the module docs
for the resolve-then-dispatch flow and the auth posture.

200.description: The resolved launch URL, for a forwarded caller's page to navigate to

204.description: Host sink opened the launch URL for a loopback caller

403.description: The caller's token doesn't cover `wildflower/launch`, or a SMART app's required client scopes

503.description: No reachable launch target (a requires_tunnel app while the tunnel is down)

delete.summary:
`DELETE /apps/{id}` — remove a cloud app. Scope-gated on `wildflower/Apps.d`
through [`Scoped<LiveAppsDeleter>`].

409.description: The app exists but is not removable (system apps)

post.summary:
`POST /cloud-apps` — create a cloud app. Scope-gated on `wildflower/Apps.c`
through [`Scoped<LiveAppsCreator>`].

get.summary:
`GET /cloud-apps/{id}` — the cloud editor detail. Scope-gated on
`wildflower/Apps.r` through [`Scoped<LiveAppsReader>`].

404.description: No cloud app has this id

put.summary:
`PUT /cloud-apps/{id}` — replace a cloud app's content. Scope-gated on
`wildflower/Apps.u` through [`Scoped<LiveAppsEditor>`].

404.description: No cloud app has this id

put.summary:
`PUT /home-screen` — atomically reorder + enable/disable every app. Scope-gated
on `wildflower/Apps.u` through [`Scoped<LiveAppsEditor>`]. The body must list
**every** registry app exactly once (its order is the new display order); a
missing / duplicated / unknown id is `400 InvalidHomeScreen`. Returns the
resulting catalogue in its new order.

200.description: The whole registry in its new order

400.description: The body wasn't an exact permutation of the registry

get.summary:
`GET /system-apps/{id}` — the system read-only detail. Scope-gated on
`wildflower/Apps.r` through [`Scoped<LiveAppsReader>`].

404.description: No system app has this id

AppKind.description:
Which kind an app is — the discriminator. Serialized as its kebab string
(`"system"` / `"cloud"`), the same value stored in the
`CHECK`-constrained `app_registrations.kind` column and sent on the wire.

AppNotEditableBody.description:
Wire shape for `AppNotEditable` (409) — the app exists but isn't editable /
removable: a system app. (A per-kind path given an id of another kind is a
`404`, not a `409` — the mismatch can't be expressed.)

AppNotFoundBody.description: Wire shape for `AppNotFound`. Matches the TS `AppNotFoundSchema`.

AppRegistration.description:
A registration row — the shared half of one app's record. Diesel maps it
to/from `app_registrations` (the [`AppKindColumn`] mapping on `kind`); serde
projects it onto the `GET /apps` wire item (`position` omitted, `client_id` →
`isSmart`).

id.description: Stable id, globally unique across all kinds (the registration PK).

kind.description: The discriminator — which configuration table holds this id's payload.

onHomescreen.description:
Whether the app's tile shows on the home screen. Curated atomically by
`PUT /home-screen` (see [`replace_placements`](super::AppsStore::replace_placements)).

subtitle.description: `None` means "no subtitle"; the wire omits an absent one.

localOnly.description: The declared no-egress flag (a UI badge this pass).

isSmart.description:
Soft reference to a gatekeeper `clients.client_id`; `None` for non-SMART
apps. Never leaves the host: the wire carries the derived `isSmart` boolean.

requiresTunnel.description:
Whether a launch must bring the tunnel up first (a launch-readiness pill).
`false` for system apps; meaningful only for cloud apps.

CloudAppBody.description:
The JSON body shared by `POST /cloud-apps` (create) and `PUT /cloud-apps/{id}`
(content replace): a cloud app's editable content. `url` is read as a raw string
so a bad value yields the structured `400 InvalidUrl` rather than a generic
deserialize error. Matches the TS `CloudAppBodySchema`.

url.description:
The launch URL template (`{origin}` / `{launch}` tokens), validated to
`400 InvalidUrl` through the write-side [`AppUrl`](crate::domain::AppUrl)
filter.

The stored launch URL template (`{origin}` / `{launch}` tokens), serialized
as its canonical string.

isRemovable.description: Always `true` for a cloud app; carried for a uniform editor contract.

CloudAppDetail.description:
The `GET`/`POST`/`PUT /cloud-apps…` wire shape — the shared registration fields
plus the stored `url` template and `isRemovable`. Built from the cloud
`(registration, configuration)` pair.

HomeScreenEntry.description:
One entry in the `PUT /home-screen` body: an app id and its desired
`onHomescreen` flag. The entry's index in the array is its new display
`position`. Matches the TS `HomeScreenEntrySchema`.

InsufficientScopeBody.description:
Wire shape for a 403 — the caller authenticated, but their token doesn't cover
the scope(s) an operation requires. `missingScopes` names the scopes the
caller must additionally hold.

error.description: Always `"InsufficientScope"` — the discriminant a client switches on.

missingScopes.description: The rendered scopes the caller lacks.

InvalidFieldBody.description:
Wire shape for a 400 carrying a discriminant + human-readable reason. Reused
for `InvalidUrl` (a bad app URL) and `InvalidName` (an empty name) — both
write-side field validations the client renders inline. The `error` discriminant lets a client
tell them apart.

InvalidHomeScreenBody.description:
Wire shape for a 400 `InvalidHomeScreen` — the `PUT /home-screen` body wasn't
an exact permutation of the registry. Matches the TS `InvalidHomeScreenSchema`.

LaunchTargetBody.description:
Wire shape of a forwarded launch's `200`: the resolved launch URL, for the
caller's page to navigate to.

url.description: The absolute launch URL (a rendered system or cloud template).

LaunchUnavailableBody.description:
Wire shape for a 503 `LaunchUnavailable` — a launch with no *reachable*
target. The SPA surfaces the failure rather than following a dead redirect.

RegistrationWire.description:
The registration fields every per-kind detail carries, `#[serde(flatten)]`ed into
each wire shape so the eight shared fields — and their `From<&AppRegistration>`
projection — are declared once rather than copied across the detail structs.
`isSmart` is derived from the host-only `client_id`; `position` never leaves the
host.

url.description:
The stored launch URL template (`{origin}` token), serialized as its
canonical string. Display-only — a system app is never editable.

SystemAppDetail.description:
The read-only `GET /system-apps/{id}` wire shape — the registration fields plus
the display-only `url` template. A system app is never editable, so it carries
no `isRemovable`.
